related_links.title: Saturday Games To Watch: SAHE, Pine Belt, Meridian and more

article.headline: Scores from last Night: SAHE turns tables on Pine Belt; Meridian girls reach 6-0
article.html:
SAHE turned the tables on Pine Belt with a 32-12 neutral-site football playoff win Saturday, November 14, while Meridian’s girls reached a listed 6-0 with a 69-18 victory over St. Martin. Starkville added a road win against Ramsay, and Biloxi and Houston kept unbeaten girls basketball starts intact. The selected soccer results brought two narrow Hernando wins against Brandon and a split for Lewisburg against the same opponent.

Football: SAHE reverses the earlier result against Pine Belt

SAHE defeated Pine Belt 32-12 in the neutral playoff game identified in our Saturday Games To Watch preview as the MSCAA Championship. The completed matchup lists the Brandon-based Warriors at 9-2 and the Hattiesburg-based Spartans at 10-2. The outcome reversed their September 19 meeting, which Pine Belt won. Saturday gave SAHE the later playoff victory after that regular-season defeat.

Girls basketball: Meridian starts fast and stays perfect

Meridian beat visiting St. Martin 69-18 and is listed at 6-0, with the Yellow Jackets at 0-3. The posted box score shows how quickly the Wildcats separated: Meridian scored 30 points in the first quarter and 29 in the second. That opening carried the hosts to another win without surrendering their perfect start.

Starkville won 55-48 at Ramsay in Birmingham, Alabama, moving to a listed 4-1 record and handing the Rams their first loss at 3-1. Biloxi also came through a close girls game, beating Bob Jones 73-66 at a neutral site. The Indians remain unbeaten at a listed 4-0, while Bob Jones is listed at 3-2.

Houston won its away tournament game at Belmont 75-58 to reach a listed 4-0 record. Belmont’s completed matchup record is 0-2. Houston joined Meridian and Biloxi among the unbeaten girls programs that extended their starts in this selection of Saturday results.

Soccer: Hernando wins twice against Brandon

Hernando took both verified varsity soccer matches against Brandon by a single goal. The boys won 2-1: the posted box score has the teams level 1-1 at halftime, with Hernando scoring the only goal after the break. The girls won 1-0, giving the Tigers a shutout alongside the boys’ narrow result.

Lewisburg split its verified matches against Brandon. The boys won 3-1 and remain unbeaten at a listed 4-0. The girls lost 3-1 and are listed at 4-1, marking their first loss. Brandon therefore recorded a win against Lewisburg’s girls alongside its other selected soccer results.
